In today’s crowded B2B landscape, capturing attention is only half the battle. Turning that attention into genuine, lasting interest in your product or service is what separates high-performing marketing teams from the rest. A solid **demand generation strategy** gives your sales team more qualified leads to work with and keeps your pipeline consistently full.


Read on to learn the **demand generation tactics** that will put you on the fast lane to growing your business.


## **What Is Demand Generation?**


Demand generation is a holistic marketing approach focused on creating long-term customer interest and engagement through strategic, multi-channel marketing campaigns. It not only aims to drive immediate sales but also to build brand awareness, positioning a brand as a trusted leader in its market.


By combining tactics like content marketing, email campaigns, events, and digital advertising, demand generation helps businesses attract new prospects, nurture relationships, and ultimately convert interest into revenue.


### Demand Generation vs Lead Generation


To add more clarity, demand generation encompasses the entire spectrum of marketing activities aimed at building long-term market enthusiasm and educating potential customers about a brand’s products or services.


In contrast, lead generation is a subset of demand generation, focused specifically on capturing information from potential customers through targeted activities like sign-ups or downloads, to create a database of prospects for direct sales efforts.


- *Learn More: Demand Generation vs Lead Generation*


## **1. Improve Demand Funnel Framework**


Think of your demand generation funnel as a map to help you better visualize the various stages of the customer journey that your audience experiences. It will keep you aware of what they go through—from the moment they first notice your brand to when they make a purchase decision.


Conducting intensive market research is critical to gaining a clearer perspective of what type of model you need to adopt for your specific industry and goals. It will enable you to tailor your demand generation campaign to your exact needs and improve your definition of a qualified lead.


To optimize your framework, you could divide it into four main phases—discovery, engagement, conversion, and reward—and go from there. However, keep in mind that there’s no one-size-fits-all formula for demand generation tactics. The approach you take should be unique to your brand, your audience, and your offering. You can assess your demand generation needs as you go and add stages to your map accordingly.


## **2. Integrate CRM & Marketing Automation**


With the many actions involved in a good demand generation strategy, it can get rather challenging to manage things on your own. Luckily, you can always lean on automation tools to get things running smoothly and do more in less time. Marketing automation can help optimize:


- Lead generation and nurturing
- Social media posts scheduling
- Analytics and reporting
- Drip email campaigns
- Search Engine Optimization
- Digital advertising
- Reputation management


In addition, marketing automation and CRM allow all parties involved in the demand generation funnel to perform their duties more efficiently. Implementing the right automated demand generation tools will take repetitive activities out of the way so that they can spend more time nurturing those prospects that are more likely to make a purchase.


## **3. Optimize Lead Nurturing**


To attract prospects and turn them into leads, you need to develop and reinforce your relationship with them at every stage in the funnel. If you listen closely to their wants and needs, you can deliver a more attractive response through your marketing and communication efforts. Giving your target audience relevant and useful information throughout the sales pipeline will help you gain their trust and build a stronger bond with them.


Now more than ever it’s important to indulge your prospects with a smooth cross-channel experience. This will make it easier for them to navigate the purchasing process and make them more likely to buy. Creating a seamless, non-invasive, and personalized advertising experience for your customers will make them feel valued and heard.


Most marketing automation platforms will allow your organization to create a solid lead-nurturing program that enables lasting relationships with potential clients through meaningful interactions. Testing these exchanges will keep them effective and healthy, and will give you valuable insights into what type of messages your leads find the most useful along with how often they want to receive them.


## **4. Refine Your Lead Scoring**


Nobody wants to waste time and resources on leads who will never take the leap and make a purchase. Lead scoring will help you ensure that the leads you’re working with are more likely to buy from you and enable you to prioritize them.


Assigning a score to your leads based on relevant data is the backbone of a solid lead-nurturing methodology. It helps you define when it’s best to reach out to each buyer, what to tell them, and how. Your lead scoring efforts should consider:


- Lead demographics and firmographics
- Budget authority, need, and time (BANT)
- Lead interest and engagement
- Lead behavior
- Social media activity


## **5. Use Account-Based Marketing (ABM)**


Focusing on an account rather than an individual lead is an excellent strategy for scalable business development and revenue growth. It allows you to combine your resources and efforts and build tailored marketing and sales tactics to drive engagement among high-value accounts.


ABM marketing uses data to pinpoint which accounts you should target. This approach gets you closer to finding the right contacts within an organization so that you can provide them with personalized communications that offer them more value.


- *Learn More: Demand Generation vs Account-Based Marketing*


## **6. Develop a Content Strategy**


Demand generation relies heavily on the content you craft to educate your audience and create brand awareness. That’s why developing a robust content strategy is so important. When you design a solid plan for content creation and publishing based on your target audience’s interests and behavior, you become more likely to get better leads and increase your sales.


Today, the vast majority of B2B marketers rely on content marketing to reach their audiences, and that investment is growing. According to recent industry data, 91% of B2B marketers use content marketing as part of their strategy, and content budgets now represent more than a quarter of total marketing spend on average. Crafting a blueprint to map out your content plan will let you ensure all the resulting materials are relevant and goal-driven. To prepare a winning content strategy, you must define:


- Your audience
- Your voice and style
- The purpose of your content
- The reaction you want to convey
- The types of content you want to create
- When and where you’ll publish it
- How you’ll promote it


## **7. Leverage Social Media**


Demand generation is all about capturing your target audience’s interest. Social media is a potent tool to achieve this goal if you know how to take advantage of its reach and versatility. This demand generation channel will give you an audience and the possibility to push your content to them organically through valuable posts. Using diverse social media platforms will help you connect and interact with your prospects, providing you with interesting insights that can be utilized to make your content more relatable.


Also, social listening will give you an endless source of relevant data on your audience’s behavior, preferences, needs, and more. This information will help you masterfully shape your demand gen campaigns to make them much more effective.


## **8. Enhance Email Marketing Efforts**


Email marketing is a valuable data source that will help you optimize your demand generation efforts. Evaluating your email marketing campaign performance based on your open rates, spam complaints, and unsubscribe rates will lead you to improve your efforts. Some actions you can take to enhance your email marketing actions are:


- Scrubbing and verifying your email list regularly
- Making your messages more relatable
- Personalizing your content to each recipient
- Segmenting your email list
- Having a clear call to action (CTA) every time
- Using responsive templates
- Testing various deployment times


## **9. Build Authority with Event Marketing**


Event marketing is an excellent way to build brand awareness and authority. It gives you the opportunity for real-time buying engagement and allows you to present your prospects with solutions quickly and dynamically. In addition, hosting an event opens the door for direct interaction with your audience. Leveraging this marketing tool will enable you to develop trust and build brand loyalty.
